issues.ko: 6×6 판에 X와 O가 번갈아 돌을 하나씩 놓는다. 돌을 놓은 자리에서 가로·세로·대각선 여덟 방향을 각각 보아, 상대 돌이 한 개 이상 빈틈없이 이어지고 그 바로 다음에 자기 돌이 있으면 그 사이의 상대 돌을 모두 뒤집어 자기 돌로 만든다. 상대 돌을 하나 이상 뒤집을 수 있는 자리에만 둘 수 있다. 둘 수 있는 자리가 없으면 차례를 넘긴다. 더 둘 곳이 없으면 돌이 많은 쪽이 이긴다.
issues.en: On a 6×6 board, X and O take turns placing one disc at a time. Looking from the square where the disc was placed in each of the eight horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions, if one or more of the opponent's discs continue without a gap and the player's own disc comes right after them, all of the opponent's discs in between are flipped to become the player's own discs. A player may play only on a square where one or more of the opponent's discs can be flipped. If there is no square to play on, the turn is passed. When there are no more places to play, the side with more discs wins.
issues.explanation: "the square where the disc was placed in each of the eight ... directions" lets the direction phrase attach to "placed"; the Korean clearly means looking in each direction from the placed square. Moving the phrase removes the misparse (apply the same change to the twin).
issues.suggested_en: On a 6×6 board, X and O take turns placing one disc at a time. Looking in each of the eight horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions from the square where the disc was placed, if one or more of the opponent's discs continue without a gap and the player's own disc comes right after them, all of the opponent's discs in between are flipped to become the player's own discs. A player may play only on a square where one or more of the opponent's discs can be flipped. If there is no square to play on, the turn is passed. When there are no more places to play, the side with more discs wins.

issues.ko: 6×6 판에 X와 O가 번갈아 돌을 하나씩 놓는다. 돌을 놓은 자리에서 가로·세로 네 방향만 각각 보아, 상대 돌이 한 개 이상 빈틈없이 이어지고 그 바로 다음에 자기 돌이 있으면 그 사이의 상대 돌을 모두 뒤집어 자기 돌로 만든다. 대각선 방향으로는 뒤집지 않는다. 상대 돌을 하나 이상 뒤집을 수 있는 자리에만 둘 수 있다. 둘 수 있는 자리가 없으면 차례를 넘긴다. 더 둘 곳이 없으면 돌이 많은 쪽이 이긴다.
issues.en: On a 6×6 board, X and O take turns placing one disc at a time. Looking from the square where the disc was placed in each of only the four horizontal and vertical directions, if one or more of the opponent's discs continue without a gap and the player's own disc comes right after them, all of the opponent's discs in between are flipped to become the player's own discs. No discs are flipped in the diagonal directions. A player may play only on a square where one or more of the opponent's discs can be flipped. If there is no square to play on, the turn is passed. When there are no more places to play, the side with more discs wins.
issues.explanation: Same misattachment as the twin, plus the awkward "each of only the four"; Korean is "네 방향만 각각 보아" (looking only in each of the four directions). Rewording keeps the twin differing only where the Korean differs.
issues.suggested_en: On a 6×6 board, X and O take turns placing one disc at a time. Looking only in each of the four horizontal and vertical directions from the square where the disc was placed, if one or more of the opponent's discs continue without a gap and the player's own disc comes right after them, all of the opponent's discs in between are flipped to become the player's own discs. No discs are flipped in the diagonal directions. A player may play only on a square where one or more of the opponent's discs can be flipped. If there is no square to play on, the turn is passed. When there are no more places to play, the side with more discs wins.
